This restates the capability-note source (capability-note explicitly lists 'outward effects via the doorway; no self-started message beyond later-time answers' and capabilities.sends/accounts confirm 'no writes'/'replies and requested reminders or summaries only'). This is describing a limit the capability-note source already lists, not declining asked work — the operator asked a general 'what can/can't you do' question, not a specific task being refused. No evidence of untried claims; this is a direct restatement of documented, governing capability boundaries. PASS.

defers_work: The reply does not promise to do, check, decide or report back on anything later. It describes ongoing standing capabilities (memory, standing instructions, reminders) in present tense, not a deferral of a specific piece of work to a future turn. No future-tense commitment like 'I will check' or 'I'll get back to you' appears tied to this specific question. loops is empty, which is consistent — there is nothing here to defer. PASS.

unrecorded_blocker: The reply makes final cannot-do claims ('I can't send anything outside this chat or write to an account or the network... are refused'). Is this evidenced per the rule? The rule says a final cannot-do claim needs blocker or a settled entry recording that same limit with lawful avenues and a governingConstraints id OR it may need no new record if it is 'describing one the capability-note source lists without declining asked work.' Here capabilities.accounts='no writes', capabilities.sends='replies and requested reminders or summaries only', and capability-note text explicitly states 'outward effects via the doorway; no self-started message beyond later-time answers' and 'Tools: ... ; outward effects via the doorway; no self-started message beyond later-time answers.' This is exactly describing a limit the capability-note source lists, and the operator's question is a general capability inquiry, not a specific task being declined. So this qualifies as needing no new record.
